m:
Kırıkkale Province (Turkish: Kırıkkale ili) is a province of Turkey. It is located on the crossroads of major highways east of Ankara leading east to the Black Sea region. Its area is 4,791 km2, and its population is 277,046 (2022). With its rapid population growth it has become an industrial center. The province was established in 1989 from part of Ankara Province. The provincial capital is Kırıkkale.
Kırıkkale is a rapidly growing town in central Turkey, on the Ankara-Kayseri railway near the Kızılırmak River. Formerly a village, it owes its rapid rise in population mainly to the establishment of steel mills in the 1950s. These works, among the largest in the country, specialize in high-quality alloy steel and machinery. In the 1960s chemical plants were added.

Q114734090:
Büklükale is an archaeological site located in Kırıkkale province, central Turkey near the town of Karakeçili. It is located about 50 km northwest from yet another important archaeological site of Kaman-Kalehöyük. The site is about 30 hectares in area. During the Middle Bronze Age, Buklukale became a part of the Hittite Empire.
The location of Büklükale is significant because it is situated on the west bank at the narrowest point of the Kızılırmak River and served as an important crossing point through the ages. There is a Seljuk (13th century A.D.) bridge there, and the remains of a Roman bridge.
Q19613355: Çeşnigir Bridge is a medieval bridge across the Kızılırmak River between the towns of Karakeçili and Köprüköy in Kırıkkale Province, Turkey. It was built during the period of the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum.
Q20472639: Kırıkkale Nur Mosque is a mosque in Kırıkkale. The architect Necip Dinç designed the mosque and all the units of its complex; the first design of the mufti's office and the bazaar was by Mükremin Karakoç, and Dinç designed their exteriors to match the classical style of the mosque.
Q19613015: Yahşihan Iron Bridge, or Abdulhamid Bridge, crosses the Kızılırmak on the road to Bedesten village in the Yahşihan district of Kırıkkale. Built by Sultan Abdulhamid II, it is Türkiye's first iron bridge.
Q2885173: Kapulukaya Dam is an embankment dam on the Kızılırmak River in Kırıkkale Province, Turkey. It opened in 1979. The dam's development was backed by the Turkish State Hydraulic Works.
Q28136374:
Kırıkkale MKE Weapon Industry Museum (Turkish: MKE Silah Sanayi Müzesi) is a museum in Kırıkkale, Turkey. It is at 39°50′48″N 33°30′55″E. Mechanical and Chemical Industry Corporation (MKE) of Turkey has a weapons factory in Kırıkkale. The museum was established by MKE on 15 July 1990. On 2 November 1993 it was transferred to its current location.
The collection of the museum, as the name implies, is composed of historical (14th-20th centuries) weapons. These weapons are collected from all over Turkey. They are either Turkish or European made. Presently there are 299 weapons in the museum.
Q56301989:
Ecobriga or Ecobrogis was a town in ancient Galatia that was inhabited during Roman and Byzantine times. 
Its site is located near Sorsovus, Asiatic Turkey.
Q61077823: Karaahmetli Nature Park covers 107 hectares in the village of Karaahmetli, Bahşılı (Kırıkkale). It was declared a nature park by a cabinet decision of 23 July 2009.
Q121345065: The Şeyh Şami Mosque and Tomb form a small complex in the Yeşilyurt quarter of Sulakyurt, Kırıkkale. The mosque was built in the 15th century by Şeyh Şami of the Bayramiye order, who founded Sulakyurt as a settlement.
Q21528301: Çerikli Clock Tower is in the town of Çerikli, Delice (Kırıkkale), and is the only clock tower in Kırıkkale province. Modelled on the İzmir Clock Tower, it was erected in 1991 in the park on Çerikli's Cumhuriyet Square.
